analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. Per the file_changes patch, it bumps the 'Last updated' date, adds one test command (scripts/test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py), and expands prose about release-publication tests for the cluster_runtime block. That block covers payload digests, malformed-block refusals, a 64 KiB registration body limit, derived-ID length limits and a local-HTTP metadata-fetch test with no network or weights. The supplied base_text units are unchanged surrounding documentation (lines 1391-2308). The changed lines 1325-1340 and 1353-1356 on the head side are not visible in the units. The patch excerpt is truncated at 'scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh ha', so the rest of the head change is unseen. I saw nothing in the unchanged text that gives a security regression. The text I could examine adds no runtime code, endpoint, secret handling, authorization path, attestation logic or prefix-cache storage behavior. It does not alter T-041 or the SSD cache posture, TB-011 authorization, TB-002 coordinator-provider websocket, or any release-registration key (A-005) or binary-hash registry (A-011) control. The documented test behavior (refusing malformed blocks, enforcing size bounds, no network) is consistent with the threat model's emphasis on strict bounded input. Remaining uncertainty: the cluster_runtime registration block and the model-metadata fetch script are described but not supplied. Their actual validation, trust of the model registry/CDN, and whether the block affects serving authorization (A-016, A-017) need review in whatever PR contains the implementation. This documentation-only change gives no evidence of a regression, but it does not clear those components.
